RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, March 13, 2012/Phalguna 23, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Drinking Water and Sanitation; Environment and Forests; Finance;
Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises;
Petroleum and Natural Gas; Rural Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Bilateral investment protection for
foreign investors
*1. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that foreign
investors are looking at the bilateral
investment protection agreements signed
with India to find a way out of the 2G
impasse;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps Ministry is taking to
remove uncertain atmosphere for foreign
investors?
Claiming of expenditure by RIL for
FDP of KG-D6 Basin
*2. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Reliance Industries Limited
(RIL) has claimed more expenditure than
incurred for the Field Development Plan
(FDP) of the D6 block at Krishna Godavari
(KG) Basin;
(b) whether any action has been taken
against RIL for the losses in revenue caused
to Government in its production sharing
contract with the company relating to the
KG Basin;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Lion as National Animal
*3. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) the population of tigers in the
country and the population of Lions in Gir
Forest of Gujarat;
(b) whether it is a fact that the existing
population of lion is available only in Gir
Forest in Asia;
(c) the reasons for Government not
changing its view and declaring 'Lion' as
the National Animal;
(d) whether tigers are available at a
number of places in Asia but the royal
animal 'Lion' is available only in Gir; and

2
(e) whether in view of this fact
Government would promote Gir as a
National tourist centre and declare 'Lion'
as the National Animal?
Millennium Development Goals for the
health sector
†*4. SHRIMA TI HEMA MALINI: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has set up Millennium Development Goals
for the health sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
achievements made so far in respect of the
targets fixed;
(c) whether Government had fixed any
target in the Eleventh Five Year Plan for
the health sector; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
achievements made so far in respect of the
target fixed?
Crops and human lives damaged by
wild animals
*5. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the increasing incidents of
damage to crops and human lives by wild
animals, including monkeys, have been
reported from various States in the country,
particularly in Himachal Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof during the
last three years and the current year, State-
wise;
(c) whether Government has provided
any compensation for loss of human lives
and crops;
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and if not, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether Government proposes to
make any provision to compensate the
victims of such incidents; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Extension of PNG network in the
country
*6. SHRI HUSAIN DALWAI: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of cities in the country,
which do have pressurized Piped Natural
Gas (PNG) supply for domestic use, State-
wise;
(b) whether there is a proposal to
provide PNG to more than 200 cities across
the country;
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(d) whether any targets have been set
for making provision of PNG in these
cities; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Economic crisis
*7. SHRI BHARATSINH
PRABHATSINH PARMAR: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has thoroughly
studied the issue of Eurozone financial
crisis, particularly the probable default of
Greece Government on debts;
(b) the steps taken by Government to
avoid such economic crisis in our country;
(c) the reasons for not accelerating dis-
investment of PSUs, as it will be helpful
in minimizing our fiscal deficit and also
boost economic development; and
(d) the target for disinvestment set by
Government for the coming three years?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

3
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Violations in clearing projects
dangerous to forests
*8. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
some members of the Statutory Forest
Advisory Committee have reportedly
pointed out certain violations in clearing
projects that are dangerous to forests;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of corrective measures
taken by Government to improve the
working of the State Forest Department

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, March 13, 2012/Phalguna 23, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Drinking Water and Sanitation; Environment and Forests;
Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Rural Development)
Total number of questions — 155
1
Toilet facilities in the country
1. SHRIMATI KUSUM RAI: Will the
Minister of DRINKING WA TER AND
SANITA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether 60 per cent of population
is forced to defecate in the open due to
absence of toilet facilities in the country as
per the recent report of a Government
panel;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the reason for such a pathetic
condition and the reaction of Government
thereto;
(d) the details of toilets constructed
under Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) in
the country during 2011 and 2012, so far,
State-wise; and
(e) the details of funds allocated and
utilized for construction of toilets during
the last three years and the current financial
year, so far, State-wise?
Establishment of Fluoride Mitigation
Centre at Gandhinagar, Gujarat
2. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR:
SHRI KANJIBHAI PA TEL:
SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN
IRANI:
Will the Minister of DRINKING
WA TER AND SANITATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in view of
the in-principle approval given by the
Ministry, the State Government of Gujarat
has submitted the proposal to establish the
Fluoride Mitigation Centre in Gandhinagar;
(b) if so, the present status of the
proposal; and
(c) by when the Fluoride Mitigation
Centre is likely to be established?
Drinking water in rural Rajasthan
3. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA:
Will the Minister of DRINKING WATER
AND SANITA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether as per the Habitation
Survey conducted in 2003, Rajasthan had
1,07,768 habitations of which 5934 were
not covered (NC), 17168 partially covered
(PC) and 34666 fully covered (FC) for
drinking water;

2
(b) whether the status of habitations,
as on 1 April, 2009 was that the State had
1,21,133 habitations of which 44,044 were
NC, 21,092 were PC and 56,001 were FC,
thus, nearly 1/3 of habitation had no assured
potable water supply in rural Rajasthan,
even after 63 years of Independence;
(c) if so, by when they are likely to be
covered;
(d) the overall scenario of rural India
regarding assured potable source of drinking
water to habitations, State-wise; and
(e) the financial outlay for Rural
Drinking Water during the past three years
and the current year?
Smart water management in Andhra
Pradesh
4. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will the
Minister of DRINKING WA TER AND
SANITATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is adopting
smart water management with some action
plan;
(b) if so, the details worked out so far,
State-wise, including Andhra Pradesh; and
(c) if not, the views of the experts in
this regard to create smart waterway which
will act as an additional reservoir for the
States besides providing irrigation facilities
in each State especially for the backward
areas in Andhra Pradesh in the Twelfth Five
Year Plan?
Safe drinking water and sanitation
facilities
5. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
DRINKING WATER AND
SANITATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 50
per cent of the Indians have no access to
safe drinking water and proper sanitation;
(b) whether any estimation has been
made to find out the total financial
requirements for providing safe drinking
water and proper sanitation facilities to all
families; and
(c) the total funds released by
Government and funds utilised during the
last three years, State wise?
Clean drinking water in rural areas
6. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of DRINKING WATER AND
SANITATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has recently
conducted a survey to identify areas in each
State/Union Territory (UT) which are
deficient in drinking water supply;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/Union
Territory-wise;
(c) whether the quality of drinking
water available in these areas is also poor;
(d) if so, the schemes launched by
Government in this regard;
(e) the targets fixed and achieved by
each State/UT during each of the last three
years under these schemes; and
(f) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
by Government to ensure supply of clean
drinking water to the rural areas of the
country?
Relocation of elephant herds in
Hassan district, Karnataka
7. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:

3

(a) whether Government has prepared
any action plan to relocate the elephant
herds in Hassan district in Karnataka to
larger elephant habitats or elephant camps;
(b) if not, by when this is likely to
happen; and
(c) the areas that have been declared as
elephant corridors?
Pollution by Okhla Waste-to-Energy
plant
8. SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAY AN
SI
